what: Autoliv makes the safety equipment inside cars: airbags, seatbelts and steering wheels. Roughly one in three cars built worldwide carries its products.
customers: Carmakers worldwide, who design its systems into vehicle platforms years before production.
money: front, side and curtain airbags and steering wheel systems
moat: Safety components are crash-tested and homologated with a specific vehicle, so they cannot be swapped mid-programme, and Autoliv has roughly 45% of a two-company global market.
risks: Revenue depends on global vehicle production volumes, which have been flat
Carmakers push for annual price reductions on every component
A 6.8% net margin leaves modest room
opportunities: 14.2 times earnings and 11.7 times free cash flow with $729M of free cash flow
Safety content per vehicle keeps rising as regulations demand more airbags
Analysts see about 11% upside, and the company buys back stock steadily
watch: Organic growth relative to global vehicle production, and the operating margin.
